newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM says cabinet agrees to confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM says cabinet agrees to confidence vote.

text.p: The Czech government decided on Wednesday to ask the lower house of parliament for a vote of confidence following a shake-up in the beleaguered cabinet and an emergency austerity package announced last week.
"The government agreed...to submit a request to parliament about an expression of confidence," Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told a news conference after a cabinet meeting.
"I will ask for this topic to be included in the agenda of the 11th session (beginning next Tuesday)," he said.
Klaus's three-party centre-right coalition holds 100 seats in the 200-member lower house and a confidence vote would require a simple majority to pass.
The government's popularity has dropped sharply amid an economic downturn and a dramatic weakening of the Czech crown which forced the central bank to float the currency.

Leaders of the ruling coalition agreed last week to an austerity package of sharp budget cuts, public sector wage freezes and steps to reduce domestic demand. Precise details have yet to be announced.

The emergency package -- and accompanying ministerial changes -- was criticised by opposition politicians and commentators and sparked numerous reports of infighting within the three coalition parties.
